ocr_screen.scope: A selected corpus of publicly available scans or volumes, catalogued before 1792. Individual copies and partial or multilingual volumes are included. The Google Books and Reception Reader facsimile checks are reported separately.
ocr_screen.method: Normalize case, accents, long s, and internal apostrophes/hyphens. Find scan pages containing advanced AND advantageous and scan pages containing glorious AND glory as whole OCR tokens. Compare their positions allowing any constant offset for front matter. Recheck gaps of 154 to 158 leaves. Separately rank local ADV, GLO and WAT vocabulary and look for the 82 researchers’ readings at a constant scan-page offset. Hits can be in definitions. Textual absence is inconclusive. Row counts and printed page numbers come only from the facsimiles.

open_items.status: Catalogue verified; no public images identified for this copy. Pages 7, 163, 422 remain unchecked. The 1785 title page explicitly dates the copy checked above. Its numbered page 486 contains a list of towns, while the Huntington record describes an extent of iii–xxxvi,485,[7] with three final advertisement leaves. The Huntington copy itself ends at page 470.

Wellcome catalogues an Edward-and-Charles-Dilly imprint as 1785. The primary scanned 1785 title above names Charles Dilly only. The identity and actual date of the Wellcome record require examination. Two London 1777 catalogue records also remain open.
